citeAs: Lu, Weifeng, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, and Bo Zhao (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv.
creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xiamen University; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen)
description: A large-scale robotic failure video question-answering dataset for failure analysis and correction. It comprises 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across diverse tasks and scenes in both simulation and real-world environments, with annotations covering task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
name: RoboFAC dataset
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To ensure annotation quality, all GPT-4o-generated outputs for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction were manually reviewed and corrected.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw videos were annotated into video QA samples for eight question types. For each question type, five question templates were provided and one template was randomly sampled when constructing a QA pair. Reference answers for task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating were directly extracted from the textual descriptions, while failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction answers were generated by GPT-4o using the video and corresponding textual description as inputs, then manually reviewed and corrected.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is designed to increase diversity by including both simulated and real-world environments, varying backgrounds and camera viewpoints, and varying object categories and scenes to promote task generalization. The paper also notes that collecting only failure patterns could cause overfitting, so they additionally collected successful trajectories to prevent models from overfitting to failure patterns.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in both simulation and real-world environments. Simulation data were collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with YCB objects and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR; failure data were generated by replacing the expert policy with error-inducing code snippets at selected substages, and each failure video was recorded with a textual description. Real-world data were collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm, with each video also accompanied by a textual description.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors report that motion planning occasionally failed, producing trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions; they manually cleaned the data and retained approximately 75% of the collected simulation data.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of robot manipulation videos paired with textual descriptions. For simulated data, descriptions include the substage where the failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, a detailed textual explanation of the error, and for pose-perturbation failures, the perturbed pose; real-world videos are likewise accompanied by corresponding textual descriptions.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that the current integration of the RoboFAC model into a VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless, and that future work should explore more natural and automated mechanisms for delivering correction suggestions; success rates in real-world use remain limited partly because the VLA model has limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: In simulation, failure trajectories were created by replacing the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at a selected substage. The dataset also introduces variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints to increase visual diversity, and for each task the authors systematically vary object categories and modify scenes to promote task generalization.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors manually performed thorough data cleaning on collected trajectories and retained approximately 75% of the collected simulation data because motion planning occasionally failed and produced trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and evaluating multimodal models on robotic failure video understanding, including task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction, and for building evaluation benchmarks assessing models’ capabilities in robotic failure reasoning and recovery.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction annotations.
